newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha weaker due to crude losses on ACCESS.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha weaker due to crude losses on ACCESS.

text.p: Naphtha prices were weaker in afternoon Tokyo trade on Friday in line with crude losses on the ACCESS after-hours trading system, traders said.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half January was assessed at $227.50/229.00. It was traded at $228.50 on Thursday.
Second-half January was quoted at $225.50/227.00, down from late Thursday's $227.00/229.00. First-half February was bid at $224.00, while offers were heard at $225.50.
In inter-month naphtha spreads, first-half January/first-half February was discussed at plus $3.50/4.50.

In physical naphtha trading, a refiner said it bought a spot cargo for its petrochemical affiliate in Kawasaki, near Tokyo, at about $5.50 above the mean of Japanese quotes for second-half December arrival.
Most second-half December cargoes were traded at around a $5.50 premium this week, traders said.

Keiyo Ethylene said it brought its ethylene centre in Chiba, Japan's largest with an annual capacity of 600,000 tonnes, back on line on Thursday. The plant had been shut since early October for a routine maintenance.
